decisions.latin: Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo: a viro iníquo éripe me … et ab homínibus iníquis éripe me
decisions.why: Three *éripe me*, each with its source named (*ab hómine malo*, *a viro iníquo*, *ab homínibus iníquis*): the erípere row's *arrancar* (as 30:16, 58:2, 58:3, 70:4 *arrancai-me da mão do pecador*). The chiasm of 139:2 (verb … source : source … verb) is kept, so the verse opens and closes on the same word, as the Latin does. The Passiontide versicle *V. Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo. R. A viro iníquo éripe me* (Preces at Prime; Passiontide None) reads each half alone. Both Brazilian Catholic versions open *Livrai-me, Senhor, do homem mau* (CNBB LH, Ave Maria; `circulation.md`) — but *livrar* is liberáre's, and the psalm's own Good Friday Tract text has *líbera me* in the second colon, so the two Latin verbs would merge.

options.label: Arrancai-me … arrancai-me
options.note: Draft. The erípere row with a source named; the chiasm kept.

options.label: Livrai-me … livrai-me
options.note: The Brazilian familiar opening (CNBB LH, Ave Maria, both Hebrew-based); *livrar* is liberáre's in this psalter (58:2 has both verbs in one verse). Refused.

options.label: Libertai-me … libertai-me
options.note: The row's verb where no source is named (68:19, 118:153); here the source is always named. Kept as the gentler option.

decisions.latin: Qui cogitavérunt iniquitátes … Qui cogitavérunt supplantáre … cogitavérunt contra me
decisions.why: The psalm has *cogitavérunt* three times, always of the enemies' plotting (ἐλογίσαντο, διελογίσαντο). The cogitáre row is *pensar em* (working), with a proposal from Pss 20, 34, 51, 61 to split: evil thing as object → *maquinar*; Ps 82:4, 6 took *maquinaram contra* as option 0 (the fourth vote). Here all three places qualify (an evil object; a hostile infinitive; *contra me*), and *pensaram contra mim* is hardly Portuguese, so one verb serves all three, as the Latin has one. MS1932 has *maquinam* / *maquinaram* at 139:3 and 139:9.

options.label: maquinaram (×3)
options.note: Draft. The split proposed in the cogitáre row, as 82:4, 82:6; MS1932's verb.

options.label: pensaram em (×3)
options.note: The row's working verb; *pensaram contra mim* at 139:9 is not idiomatic, and *pensaram em iniquidades* is weak where the Latin means 'devised'.

options.label: tramaram (×3)
options.note: CNBB LH and Ave Maria *tramam o mal*; but *tramar* is concinnáre's (D44). Refused.

decisions.why: *constitúere* is *estabelecer* in the glossary, but *estabelecer batalhas* is not Portuguese; the Greek παρετάσσοντο πολέμους is 'drew up battles in array'. *armar* is the Portuguese verb for setting up a fight or a trap (MS1932 *armam combates*), and keeps the imperfect's repetition ('all day they kept setting up'). A local departure from the row, recorded. *prǽlium → batalha* (17:35, 23:8, 26:3b), kept apart from *bellum → guerra* in 139:8.

options.label: armavam
options.note: Draft. MS1932's verb; idiomatic for a fight.

options.label: dispunham
options.note: Closest to the array of the Greek; bookish.

options.label: estabeleciam
options.note: The constitúere row; not idiomatic with *batalhas*.

decisions.why: *sicut serpéntis* is a genitive: 'like (the tongue) of a serpent' (ὡσεὶ ὄφεως). *como a da serpente* keeps the genitive, as 57:5 *semelhante ao da serpente*; *como serpente* (CNBB LH, Ave Maria) makes the men the serpents. *acúere → afiar*, as 63:4 *afiaram as suas línguas como espada*. The second colon is 13:3b's third colon word for word (*venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum* → *veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios*; = Rom 3:13), verbless as the Latin.

options.label: como a da serpente
options.note: Draft. The genitive kept (57:5's build).

options.label: como as da serpente
options.note: Agrees in number with *línguas*; a serpent has one tongue.

options.label: como a serpente
options.note: CNBB LH *Como a serpente eles afiam suas línguas*; plainer, but drops the genitive.

decisions.why: The supplantáre row has *derrubar* (17:40; 36:31 *os seus passos não serão derrubados*, where *tropeçar* has no passive) and itself notes that 139:5, with *gressus* as object of an active verb, 'can still take *fazer tropeçar*'. *Derrubar os meus passos* knocks down steps; *fazer tropeçar os meus passos* is the heel-trip the word is made of (sub-planta), and pairs with the *tropeço* (scándalum) of 139:6. **v2:** the stylist heard *tropeçar* (5b) and *tropeço* (6) as one root twice where the Latin has two words (*supplantáre / scándalum*) — an echo the Latin does not have. The row's *derrubar* taken.

options.label: derrubar
options.note: v2 (stylist). The row's verb (17:40, 36:31); keeps supplantáre apart from scándalum → *tropeço* in 139:6.

options.label: fazer tropeçar
options.note: Draft 1. The heel-trip of the word, but it echoes *tropeço* (scándalum) in the next verse, which the Latin does not.

decisions.why: *in láqueum*: *in* with the accusative of purpose or result, 'into a snare, to serve as a snare' (DRB 'for a snare'; the Greek has παγίδας τοῖς ποσίν μου, 'snares for my feet', which the Gallican does not carry). *em laço* keeps the preposition and the noun, as 68:23 *Torne-se … em laço*; *como laço* is plainer and makes the purpose a comparison. *funes → cordas* (15:6, 118:61); *láqueus → laço*. MS1932 *para me surpreender* explains.

options.label: em laço
options.note: Draft. The Latin's *in*; 68:23's build.

options.label: como laço
options.note: Plainer; *in* read as 'as'.

options.label: para um laço
options.note: DRB 'for a snare'.

decisions.why: God's *virtus* → *poder* (the row; 45:2 *refúgio e poder*); *vigor* is for a man's own strength, *força* is fortitúdo's. The phrase is also the Thursday Vespers antiphon (*Ne derelínquas me, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ*) and closes the Matins antiphon / Quad2-3 Introit *Inténde in adjutórium meum … virtus salútis meæ*, so it will be said often. DRB 'the strength of my salvation'; MS1932 *fortaleza*; the CNBB LH paraphrases (*meu auxílio poderoso*).

options.label: poder
options.note: Draft. The virtus row for God.

options.label: força
options.note: DRB 'strength'; warmer in the mouth, but fortitúdo's word.

decisions.latin: Ne tradas me, Dómine, a desidério meo peccatóri
decisions.why: The crux of the psalm. The Latin follows the Greek (ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας μου ἁμαρτωλῷ), which misread the Hebrew ('grant not the desires of the wicked'). *a desidério meo* can be 'away from my desire' (deprive me of what I long for and hand me to the sinner) or 'against my desire' (MS1932 *contra o meu desejo*). DRB keeps it bare: 'Give me not up, O Lord, from my desire to the wicked.' The draft keeps it as open as the Latin: *do meu desejo ao pecador*, from one to the other. The Good Friday Tract has the same words. **v2:** the stylist asked the order *Não me entregueis ao pecador, Senhor, do meu desejo*; refused — *Senhor, do meu desejo* is then heard as a vocative ('Lord of my desire'), a reading the Latin does not have. The ambiguity reader let *do meu desejo* pass as noise: the Latin's own opacity (DRB keeps it bare); *contra o meu desejo* stays the option that resolves it.

options.label: do meu desejo
options.note: Draft. DRB's literal build; open as the Latin.

options.label: contra o meu desejo
options.note: MS1932; resolves the ambiguity.

options.label: longe do meu desejo
options.note: The separative reading made explicit; resolves the other way.

decisions.why: *ne forte* (μήποτε) → *para que não* (78:10); 90:12 has *para que não venhas a …* for the 'perchance'. *exaltári* → *exaltar-se* (the exaltáre row; 65:7 *não se exaltem*). The colon is long already (the Latin's is too); the short form is ruled. **v2:** both the Latinist and the stylist missed *forte*; *acaso* restores it.

options.label: para que acaso não se exaltem

forms.neforte: para que acaso não se exaltem

options.note: v2. *forte* carried by *acaso* — the Latinist (minor: 'forte is dropped', fix *porventura*) and the stylist (*acaso*) both asked for it; *acaso* is the plainer word, +2 syllables.

options.label: para que não se exaltem
options.note: Draft 1. Drops *forte* (Latinist minor).

options.label: para que não venham a exaltar-se

forms.neforte: para que não venham a exaltar-se

options.note: Carries *forte* as 90:12 does; +3 syllables.

options.label: para que porventura não se exaltem

forms.neforte: para que porventura não se exaltem

options.note: The Latinist's fix; *porventura* is heavier and bookish.

decisions.latin: Caput circúitus eórum: labor labiórum ipsórum opériet eos
decisions.why: *labor* (κόπος) here is what the lips work — mischief, the trouble they cause — which returns to cover them. The labor row is *fadiga* (open), with a local departure *trabalho(s)* where the noun is the product of toil (77:46, 127:2). *a fadiga dos seus lábios* is heard as tired lips. The first colon stays verbless, as the Latin (*Caput circúitus eórum*, 'the head of their encircling'; DRB 'The head of them compassing me about'); *cerco* is *circúitus* (L&S 'a going round, a circling'); MS1932 builds a sentence with *cairá* and a gloss. **v2:** the stylist heard *o trabalho dos lábios* as 'a job description' and asked the row's *fadiga* (toil, trouble); the ambiguity reader heard *o trabalho* simply as 'what they said'. The row's word taken: it keeps the toil of *labor*, and the psalter's other *labor* are *fadiga*.

options.label: a fadiga
options.note: v2 (stylist). The labor row's word (9:28, 72:5, 89:10).

options.label: o trabalho
options.note: Draft 1. The row's local departure for a product of toil; heard by the stylist as a job, by the ambiguity reader as mere speaking.

options.label: a maldade
options.note: The Hebrew's sense (CNBB *a malícia*); explains. Refused.

decisions.latin: Cadent super eos carbónes, in ignem deícies eos
decisions.why: *carbónes → carvões* (the row; 17:9, 17:13, 119:4 — the row names this verse). *brasas* (DM1962, Ave Maria *carvões ardentes*) is the row's option, to be taken for the whole row if at all. *deícere → abater* (the row, 36:14b, the same Greek καταβάλλω); *in ignem* is accusative, 'into the fire', and *no fogo* after *abater* carries the motion in Portuguese. *in misériis* (ταλαιπωρίαις) → *nas misérias*; *subsístere → subsistir* (102:16). **v2:** *no fogo os abatereis* → *ao fogo os lançareis* (Latinist minor: *in ignem* is motion into; stylist: *abater* heard as slaughter) — a local departure from the deícere row, recorded there.

options.label: carvões … ao fogo os lançareis
options.note: v2. The Latinist (minor: *in ignem* + *deícies* is motion, 'cast down into the fire'; *no fogo os abatereis* reads as striking them while in it) and the stylist (*abater* is to fell or slaughter) both asked *lançar*. A local departure from the deícere row (*abater*, 36:14b), where the object is a man struck down, not thrown into something.

options.label: carvões … abatereis
options.note: Draft 1. Both rows; the motion of *in ignem* weakened (Latinist).

options.label: brasas … abatereis
options.note: The carbónes row's option (119:4 decision `carbonibus`).

options.label: carvões … lançareis
options.note: Plainer with *no fogo*; loses the downward stroke of *de-jícere*.

decisions.latin: Vir linguósus non dirigétur in terra
decisions.why: *linguósus* (γλωσσώδης), a psalter hapax: L&S 'talkative, loquacious'. *linguarudo* keeps the tongue the Latin names and means one who talks too much, as the word does; it is everyday Brazilian, perhaps a shade familiar. DRB 'a man full of tongue'; MS1932 *O caluniador* explains; Almeida *homem de má língua* is the Hebrew's 'man of tongue' made evil. *dirigétur → será dirigido*, the dirígere row (36:23, 101:29), keeps the Latin's image of a straight course (κατευθυνθήσεται); MS1932 *não prosperará* and Almeida *não terá firmeza* are the sense. **v2:** *linguarudo* → *de língua solta* (stylist, ambiguity reader); *dirigido* held.

options.label: de língua solta … dirigido
options.note: v2 (stylist). The tongue kept; the idiom means one who talks too much and without restraint — L&S 'talkative, loquacious' — without the comic register.

options.label: linguarudo … dirigido
options.note: Draft 1. The stylist: a gossip's word, half comic, will draw a smile in choir; the ambiguity reader listed it unknown and heard 'a gossip'.

options.label: falador … dirigido
options.note: L&S's sense; loses the tongue.

options.label: de má língua … firmado
options.note: Almeida's build; adds *má*, the Hebrew's reading. Refused.

options.label: de língua solta … firmado
options.note: The stylist: *dirigido* suggests driving or directing; *firmado* is the sense (Almeida *não terá firmeza*). Refused: the dirígere row (36:23, 101:29) keeps the Latin's image of a straight course; *firmar* is stabilíre's (20:12). The ambiguity reader heard 'will not be guided' — a reading the Latin allows.

decisions.latin: virum injústum mala cápient in intéritu
decisions.why: *cápere* (θηρεύσει, 'hunt down') → *tomar*, the row (58:4 *tomaram a minha alma*, the same Greek). The Latin puts the object first; Portuguese puts the subject first (order, D2). *in intéritu* is ablative, 'in destruction' (the Greek's εἰς διαφθοράν is 'unto'); *intéritus → destruição* (9:16a *na destruição*). *vir* in both colons → *homem*, as *homo* in 139:2; Portuguese has no plain second word (*varão* would need a footnote).

options.label: os males tomarão … na destruição

forms.capient: os males tomarão o homem injusto

options.note: Draft. The cápere and intéritus rows; the ablative kept.

options.label: os males apanharão … para a destruição

forms.capient: os males apanharão o homem injusto

options.note: DRB 'shall catch … unto destruction'; the hunt's verb; *apanhar* was colloquial to the 58:4 stylist.

options.label: os males se apoderarão do homem injusto … na destruição

forms.capient: os males se apoderarão do homem injusto

options.note: MS1932's verb.

options.label: os males apanharão … na ruína

forms.capient: os males apanharão o homem injusto

options.note: The stylist ('tomarão … na destruição' flat, -ção drags). Refused: *ruína* is præcipitátio's (51:6) and intéritus is *destruição* in 9:16a, 34:7, 48:11, 54:24, 102:4; *apanhar* was colloquial to the 58:4 stylist (the same Greek θηρεύω).

decisions.latin: Cognóvi quia fáciet Dóminus judícium ínopis: et vindíctam páuperum
decisions.why: *Cognóvi* with a clause and no time-word → *sei* (the proposal in the cognóscere + *quóniam* row; DRB 'I know', MS1932 *Sei*). *judícium ínopis … vindíctam páuperum*: two genitives, the needy man's cause and the poor men's vindication (τὴν κρίσιν τοῦ πτωχοῦ καὶ τὴν δίκην τῶν πενήτων). *fará o juízo do carente* keeps the noun (judícium → juízo, D15) and the genitive, which leaves open, as the Latin does, whether the judgment is *for* him — the risk is that it is heard as judgment *on* him; *fará justiça ao carente* (MS1932) resolves it with justítia's word. *inops → carente* (D38). *vindícta → vingança* (57:11).

options.label: Eu sei … o juízo do carente
options.note: Draft. Nouns and genitives kept.

options.label: Eu sei … justiça ao carente
options.note: MS1932, DRB 'do justice to the needy'; clear, but justítia's word for judícium.

options.label: Conheci … o juízo do carente
options.note: The Latin's perfect; read as 'I met' (cognóvi row).

options.label: Eu sei … o juízo do desvalido
options.note: The stylist: *carente* is the word of social services and pop psychology. Refused under D38 (settled; *desvalido* was unknown to one reader); the ambiguity reader also named the emotional sense as audible — more evidence for D38's known cost.

decisions.latin: obumbrásti super caput meum in die belli
decisions.why: obumbráre → *fazer sombra a* (90:4); *super* kept as *sobre*. The stylist found the colon long (+4) and *sombra sobre* heavy, and asked *cobristes de sombra*. Refused: *cobrir* is opéríre's in 139:10 (*os cobrirá*), two verses on, so the Latin's two verbs would merge; and the ambiguity reader heard 'you sheltered my head' first. His line is an option; *fizestes sombra à minha cabeça* (the row's regency, −1 syllable, *super* lost) is another.

options.label: fizestes sombra sobre
options.note: Draft. The row, with *super*.

options.label: cobristes de sombra
options.note: The stylist; merges with *opériet* → *cobrirá* (139:10).

options.label: fizestes sombra à
options.note: The row's regency (*fazer sombra a*); shorter, *super* lost.

decisions.latin: et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo
decisions.why: *cum vultu tuo* → *com o vosso rosto*, word for word 15:11 and 20:7 (σὺν τῷ προσώπῳ). The stylist ('not idiomatic; *com o* blurs into *como*') asked *junto ao vosso rosto*; the ambiguity reader heard 'in your presence' first, though 'strange'. Refused: the formula of 15:11 and 20:7 has held; *junto a* is *juxta*'s (139:6). Option.

options.label: junto ao vosso rosto
options.note: The stylist; *junto* is juxta's in 139:6.

choices.139:2: No title line (*In finem, Psalmus David*): DO's Latin has none; D7. *homo malus → homem mau*; *vir iníquus → homem iníquo* (17:49 *do homem iníquo me arrancareis*). The Latin's *homo / vir* variation cannot be kept (*varão* would need a footnote). Each colon reads alone (the Passiontide versicle).
choices.139:3: *Qui* → *Os que*, a substantive relative after the singular *homem iníquo*, as the Latin's plural *qui* turns to the whole band. *tota die → o dia todo* (D24). *in corde → no coração*.
choices.139:4: The second colon copies 13:3b exactly (glossary formula row, = Rom 3:13). The ambiguity reader listed *áspides* unknown; the formula (13:3b, Rom 3:13) is kept.
choices.139:5: = the Offertory of Tuesday in Holy Week (Quad6-2), word for word. *de manu peccatóris → da mão do pecador* (70:4).
choices.139:5b: The Latin's colon at the end is kept; the sentence runs into 139:6. *abscondérunt … láqueum mihi → esconderam um laço para mim* (30:5, 34:7 *esconderam para mim*; 118:110 *puseram um laço para mim*). *supérbi → os soberbos* (118:51, 78, 122).
choices.139:6: *juxta iter → junto do caminho* (*juxta* of place → *junto de*, 5:6, 37:12b; iter → caminho). *scándalum → tropeço* (the row); *mihi → para mim*, as 5b. v2: 5b's *derrubar* removes the *tropeçar / tropeço* echo.
choices.139:7: *Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu* = 15:1 (*Eu disse ao Senhor: Vós sois o meu Deus*); *vocem deprecatiónis meæ → a voz da minha prece* (27:2, 27:6, 65:19, 85:6, 129:2b; D35).
choices.139:8: *Dómine, Dómine* both kept. *obumbrásti super caput meum → fizestes sombra sobre a minha cabeça* (obumbráre → fazer sombra a, 90:4; *super* kept). *in die belli → no dia da guerra* (77:9); *bellum → guerra* apart from *prǽlium → batalha* (139:3).
choices.139:9: Three clauses in the second colon, as the Latin; a semicolon after *contra mim* so that *não me abandoneis* is heard as a new plea. *ne derelínquas me → não me abandoneis* (26:9b, 37:22). *trádere → entregar* (118:121 *não me entregueis aos que me caluniam*).
choices.139:10: The first colon verbless, as the Latin; *seu* is theirs (God is *vosso* in this psalter). *opériet → cobrirá*.
choices.139:13: *Eu* supplied so the colon does not open on a bare verb that could be heard as a question; the subject is in the Latin's ending.
choices.139:14: *Verúmtamen → Todavia* (the row). *confitebúntur nómini tuo → darão graças ao vosso nome* (D5). *cum vultu tuo → com o vosso rosto*, word for word 15:11, 20:7 (the Latin's *cum*, σὺν τῷ προσώπῳ; CNBB *junto a vós*, Ave Maria *em vossa presença* explain). *recti → os retos* (the rectus row). This verse closes the Good Friday Tract.
choices.139:11: The second colon in the natural order (*não subsistirão nas misérias*; D2): in the Latin's order it ended on *subsistirão*, which rhymed with *destruição* at the end of 139:12, an echo the Latin (*subsístent / intéritu*) does not have. *in misériis → nas misérias* (ταλαιπωρίαις). The ambiguity reader listed *subsistirão* unknown; kept (102:16; the Latin's word).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps139.md, L&S (*linguósus* 'talkative', *circúitus* 'a circling'), and precedent by concordance (`ps139/concord.py`, adapted from ps137's): erípere (30:16, 58:2–3, 70:4), 13:3b's venom colon, 63:4 *afiaram as suas línguas*, 57:5 *ao da serpente*, láqueus / funes / scándalum / supplantáre (36:31 and the row's note on this verse), cogitáre (82:4 *maquinaram contra*), virtus (God's → poder), obumbráre (90:4), carbónes (the row names 139:11), cápere (58:4, the same Greek), intéritus, *cum vultu tuo* (15:11, 20:7). Liturgical use by grep and Brazilian circulation fetched, not asserted (`circulation.md`: the Good Friday Tract, the Holy Tuesday Offertory, the Passiontide versicle, the Thursday Vespers antiphon; CNBB LH and Ave Maria open *Livrai-me, Senhor, do homem mau*). Hard readings: 139:9 *a desidério meo* (kept open), 139:10 *Caput circúitus eórum* (verbless, kept), 139:12 *linguósus* (hapax), 139:13 *judícium ínopis* (genitive kept).

Hard checks pass. Soft flags: 139:11/139:12 finals rhymed (*subsistirão / destruição*) — mended by the natural order in 139:11. 139:5b/139:6 finals both *para mim*: the Latin's own echo (*láqueum mihi / posuérunt mihi*), kept. Length: 139:12 first colon +5 (*vir* and the future passive need *O homem … não será dirigido*; *linguarudo* is one word for one), 139:8 second colon +4 (*fazer sombra* is two words for *obumbráre*, and *sobre* keeps *super*), 139:6 second colon +3 (*para mim* as in 5b) — accepted. Shorter colons (139:2a −3, 139:7b −4, 139:10b −3) are the Latin's longer words.
2 minors, both taken. Overall: close and faithful; the hard readings (*do meu desejo ao pecador*, *A cabeça do seu cerco*, *com o vosso rosto*) kept without smoothing.

outcomes.remark: *forte* dropped; *para que porventura não se exaltem*
outcomes.reason: Taken with the stylist's plainer *acaso*; *porventura* kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: *in ignem deícies* is motion; *ao fogo os lançareis*

audit.note: 11 remarks in 7 verses; best 139:7, worst 139:12. 5 taken, 6 refused and kept as options.

outcomes.remark: *tropeçar* / *tropeço* invent a repetition; *derrubar*
colon long, *sombra sobre*; *cobristes de sombra*
outcomes.reason: *cobrir* is opéríre's in 139:10; the two Latin verbs would merge.

outcomes.remark: order hard to parse; *Não me entregueis ao pecador, Senhor, do meu desejo*
outcomes.reason: *Senhor, do meu desejo* is heard as a vocative ('Lord of my desire').

*o trabalho dos lábios* a job description; *a fadiga*
*abater* is fell or slaughter; *lançareis*
*linguarudo* comic; *de língua solta*
*dirigido* = driving; *firmado*
outcomes.reason: The dirígere row keeps the image of a straight course; *firmar* is stabilíre's.

outcomes.remark: *tomarão … na destruição* flat; *apanharão … na ruína*
outcomes.reason: intéritus → *destruição* across the psalter; *ruína* is præcipitátio's; *apanhar* was colloquial at 58:4.

outcomes.remark: *carente* social-work word; *desvalido*
outcomes.reason: D38 settled *carente*; recorded as further evidence of its cost.

outcomes.remark: *habitar com o rosto* not idiomatic; *junto ao vosso rosto*
outcomes.reason: The formula of 15:11, 20:7; *junto* is juxta's in 139:6.

audit.note: 26 items, 4 unknown words (*áspides*, *iníquo*, *subsistirão*, *linguarudo*). The real findings: 139:9 *do meu desejo* heard as noise, 139:10 *A cabeça do seu cerco* opaque — both the Latin's own opacity, kept; *linguarudo* heard as 'a gossip' (mended with the stylist); *carente*'s emotional sense audible (D38's cost). First hearings otherwise right (139:8 sheltered, 139:13 justice for the needy, 139:14 in your presence).

outcomes.remark: *Os que maquinaram* can wait for a verb
outcomes.reason: Heard first as a description of the men of 139:2, as the Latin's *Qui*.

outcomes.remark: *do meu desejo* unclear, passes as noise
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own crux, kept open (DRB bare); *contra o meu desejo* is the option that resolves it.

outcomes.remark: *A cabeça do seu cerco* has no clear sense; syntax open
outcomes.reason: The Latin's verbless colon (DRB keeps it); explaining it would add a verb or a gloss (MS1932).

outcomes.remark: *o trabalho dos seus lábios* = what they said
outcomes.reason: Changed to *a fadiga* with the stylist.

outcomes.remark: *linguarudo* unknown / a gossip
*não será dirigido* heard as 'not guided'
outcomes.reason: A reading the Latin allows; the dirígere row.

outcomes.remark: *carente* emotional sense audible
*o juízo do carente* could be judgment on him
outcomes.reason: Heard first as justice for the needy; the genitive is the Latin's.

*subsistirão* unknown

audit.note: v2: 139:5b *fazer tropeçar* → *derrubar* (stylist; the row); 139:9 *para que acaso não se exaltem* (Latinist + stylist); 139:10 *o trabalho* → *a fadiga* (stylist; the row); 139:11 *no fogo os abatereis* → *ao fogo os lançareis* (Latinist + stylist); 139:12 *linguarudo* → *de língua solta* (stylist, ambiguity reader). 139:8 and 139:14 reworded as slots only, text unchanged. Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.

v2: hard checks pass. 139:9 second colon now +3 (*acaso* restores *forte*; three clauses as the Latin); 139:12 first colon +5 (*de língua solta* for one word, and *O homem … não será dirigido*); 139:8 +4 and 139:6 +3 as in v1; the 5b/6 *para mim* echo is the Latin's (*mihi / mihi*). Accepted.

Gate on v2: no majors, 1 minor, refused with a reason. Overall: close and literal; the hard readings (v. 9 *a desidério meo peccatóri*, v. 10 *caput circúitus eórum*, v. 14 *cum vultu tuo*) kept without smoothing toward the Hebrew; tenses, persons, moods and mediants preserved.

outcomes.remark: minor: *derrubar* blurs the heel-trip of *supplantáre*; *fazer tropeçar os meus passos*
outcomes.reason: v1 had *fazer tropeçar*; the stylist heard *tropeçar* (5b) and *tropeço* (6b, scándalum) as one root twice, which merges two Latin words the psalm keeps apart. *Derrubar* is the supplantáre row's verb, and with *gressus* it matches 36:31 *os seus passos não serão derrubados*, which passed its gate. Readers pulled both ways on a minor, so the row is held; *fazer tropeçar* stays as option 1.
